item: A persisted rollup refresh that opened no connection is no build: it is not reported as built and does not end a failure run
refs: R267; audit 0.5.0; 0.5.1 item 28 read note; PR pending
summary: The independent read of #1510 noted that _refresh_persisted_build returns early when columnar.connect gives no connection (the passphrase or the secure backend vanished between the verdict and the call), and the dispatcher then fell through to _release_stopped(), reset the failure run and reported built, though nothing was refreshed. The function now returns False in exactly that case (True after a refresh; the existing stubs return None and still count as a refresh) and the dispatcher treats a False as a decline: no build ran, the outcome is declined, last_skip names persisted-unavailable, a held failure and its run stand, and the in-memory path takes over on the next kick. Two tests in tests/test_rollup_persisted_failure_hold.py: the no-connection case (outcome, last_skip, failure run kept, no hold kept) and the negative space (True and None still build); red-without by two mutations (the check skipped: 7 tests; a truthiness check instead of is-False: 2). STATED: the no-connection path is reached only on the dormant persisted store, so it is read from code and exercised through a stub, like #1510's; the check is for an explicit False so a refresh stub that returns nothing stays a build.
